Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1202
Claimant:
Rachel Wallace
Adjuster:
Christopher Wong
9-1-24
Insured reported a rear-end collision at a stop on a city street. The claimant, who is not represented by an attorney,
says they were struck from behind and felt neck pain shortly afterward.
9-5-24
Reviewed the ploicy and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is named on it. Coverage was in force at the time
of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.
9-28-24
Spoke with the claimant, who described the impact the same way as in the first report. They reported whiplash
symptoms and said they have been seen at a clinic.
10-5-24
Received photos of the rear bumper and trunk of the claimant's vehicle. The damage is consistent with the impact
described, and the photos show some of the scene details the claimant mentioned.
11-1-24
Obtained the police report. The officer and two bystanders who spoke at the scene state that the claimant was not
inside the vehicle when the collision occurred, which conflicts with the claimant's account. No independent witness
has been identified who can confirm the claimant's position.
11-14-24
Called the claimant to ask about the conflict in the accounts. They repeated the same description of the crash and
said they had stepped out briefly before the collision, without changing any other detail.
11-18-24
Reviewed the medical records received so far. The whiplash diagnosis is plausible for a collision of this type, and no
prior injury to the neck or upper back appears in the claimant's history. Treatment has continued somewhat longer
than is typical for this injury.
1-29-25
Checked prior claims and vehicle history for the claimant's car. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and
nothing indicates an earlier injury claim involving the same body area.
2-28-25
Summarized the file for supervisor review. Medical treatment duration and the disputed position of the claimant at
impact remain open items, and the damage and injury evidence are otherwise consistent with the reported loss. Next
step is to request the teratment billing and a recorded statement from the claimant.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
